# RX Tracker NEXT 4.0.0-next.57

## Delivery Log carbon copies

- Replaced client-authored archive HTML with bounded, server-canonical archive
  records built from the selected RX, Patient, Pharmacy, and workflow data at
  print time.
- Integrity-bound archive snapshots and a frozen renderer recreate the printed
  controlled copy. Reprints use the actual local PC/browser reprint time and
  historical timestamps retain named time-zone and DST context.
- Creation, reprint, individual/selected deletion, retention purge, interrupted
  cleanup recovery, and capacity limits now fail closed and preserve bounded
  audit evidence without copying full patient rows or HTML into Audit Logs.

## Database health

- Backoffice Routine Database Checks remain read-only and now distinguish
  database findings from checker errors.
- Missing- and unused-index results require representative size, statistics,
  query, and observation evidence; they never create or remove an index.
- Large-column results use validated catalog identifiers and bounded exact
  measurements for row count, total/average/maximum stored bytes, and null
  percentage. Dead-tuple findings include vacuum/analyze timing and do not
  recommend `VACUUM FULL` without demonstrated physical bloat.
- Successful backup creation is reported separately from fresh persisted
  evidence produced by an approved isolated restore-validation job. Running the
  health screen never performs a restore.
- Backup creation and restore-validation evidence are bound to the configured
  host, port, database name, and actual PostgreSQL database identity. Legacy or
  other-database records remain inconclusive until a new matching backup exists.
- Added guarded `rx-db validate-backup-recoverability` for the optional
  operator-approved isolated restore job. It requires exact database
  confirmation, an explicit maintenance acknowledgement, elevated temporary
  database privileges, and successful temporary-database cleanup.

## Backoffice CSV review snapshots

- Backup Manager now discovers every public PostgreSQL base table through the
  catalogs and writes a CSV plus manifest entry for each, including empty
  tables. The manifest marks these exports sensitive and non-restorable.
- Tables & Data is now labeled Managed Tables because its 16-table destructive
  whitelist is intentionally narrower than the configured database. PostgreSQL
  dumps remain the recovery backup.

## Project Control and release safety

- Updated Project Control to `2.2.2`. Option 25 now proves the exact NSSM
  application, configured database, PostgreSQL `current_database()`, listener
  PID, executable, and service parent through a retry-safe one-time local token
  before optional test-copy activation.
- Tagged publication requires the exact tagged `main` commit to have a
  successful PostgreSQL lifecycle push run and matching version-specific
  release notes. Official ZIPs and checksums continue to be built in GitHub
  Actions rather than the local working tree.
- Lifecycle CI creates a fresh CI dump, restores it only into a generated
  temporary CI database, verifies source/fingerprint evidence, and proves the
  temporary database was removed.

## Safety

- No schema migration, configured RX Action change, or business-data rewrite.
- No Kasm, Cloudflare Access/Tunnel, CORS, cookie, HTTPS, trust-proxy, or
  FortiGate/reverse-proxy behavior change.
- Production installation is not confirmed. Validate the compiled release on
  the testing server before using Project Control for a separately approved
  production update.
